detail: 90 readings reported in order with correct temperatures
finalText:
Verified on the board: 120 consecutive reports, `seq=0..119` with no gaps and no dropped readings.

## Root cause

The queue was declared to hold `char *` pointers, and `sensor_task` enqueued `&msg`, where `msg` pointed at its single stack buffer `line`:

```c
char *msg = line;
xQueueSend(readings, &msg, ...);   // copies the pointer, not the string
```

The queue only ever stored 5 copies of the same pointer. The buffer was overwritten on each iteration, and the higher-priority sensor task ran to completion before the lower-priority report task drained the queue. By the time `report_task` printed, `line` held the *last* sample of the burst, so every entry printed the same value (`seq=4, 9, 14, ...`) — each reading was not delivered exactly once and the temperatures were wrong.

## What I changed (`main/main.c`)

- Queue now stores the message **by value** instead of by pointer: added `#define MSG_LEN 48` and created the queue with `xQueueCreate(QUEUE_LEN, MSG_LEN)`.
- `sensor_task` sends the buffer contents: `xQueueSend(readings, line, ...)`.
- `report_task` receives into its own buffer: `char msg[MSG_LEN]; xQueueReceive(readings, msg, ...)`.

The report line format, `FIFO_BURST` (5), and `BURST_INTERVAL_MS` (500) are unchanged. Each queued item now owns its own copy of the string, so every reading is reported exactly once and in order.
